meta.title: Software provenance of the HVR_OPT final-closure study
meta.method: Every developer / what-it-is statement is backed by an official page fetched with curl on the date given; each quote is verbatim (whitespace collapsed) and was machine-checked against the fetched copy. In-house tools are quoted from their repository source file. Versions were probed on this host with the commands listed in version_probe. Usage claims are backed by evidence_paths (repository files).

tools.name: CalculiX (ccx)
tools.developer: Guido Dhondt (finite element solver, CalculiX CrunchiX) and Klaus Wittig (pre- and post-processor, CalculiX GraphiX)
tools.what_it_is: A free, open-source three-dimensional finite element program whose solver (ccx) does linear and non-linear static, dynamic and thermal analyses.
tools.quote: Copyright (C) 1998 Guido Dhondt and Klaus Wittig

supplementary_sources.quote: A Free Software Three-Dimensional Structural Finite Element Program
CalculiX is a package designed to solve field problems. The method used is the finite element method.
The solver is able to do linear and non-linear calculations. Static, dynamic and thermal solutions are available.
Authors: Guido Dhondt (Finite Element Solver) Klaus Wittig(Pre- and Postprocessor)
Available downloads for the solver (CalculiX CrunchiX: ccx)

tools.role_in_study: Production solver for every package thermal and mechanical result: the steady conjugate thermal FE solve (C3D8) inside the electrothermal fixed point; one thermoelastic structural solve (C3D8I) on the converged temperature field (ITERATIVE CHOLESKY on the refined production mesh, checked against the SPOOLES direct solver on the base mesh); and the local solder viscoplastic submodel (*VISCO with *CREEP, LAW=NORTON) at the critical joint. Also the production side of the thermal-column and bilayer benchmarks.

tools.name: In-house package-network FV solver
tools.developer: this study (in-house Python in this repository)
tools.what_it_is: A cell-centred finite-volume model of the package high-voltage redistribution sheet and BGA balls, solved with SciPy sparse direct solves.
tools.quote: A cell-centred finite-volume discretisation on a tensor grid whose control-volume FACES lie exactly on every tile edge
tools.source_note: in-house code: quoted from the repository source file, read on the date given
tools.role_in_study: Production model of the package HV network: per-ball current split, effective resistance, pad drops and the exhaustive ball-count screen; its output feeds the electrical ledger.

tools.name: In-house electrical ledger
tools.developer: this study (in-house Python in this repository)
tools.what_it_is: A Python bookkeeping model that lists every conductor in the power path once, with its resistance at its own temperature and the loss it deposits in each FE tier.
tools.quote: Every conductor in the Z1/Z2 power path appears exactly once, with its geometry, current type, scenario, resistance model, resistance at its own temperature, loss, the FE tier its heat is deposited in, and its evidence class.
tools.source_note: in-house code: quoted from the repository source file, read on the date given
tools.role_in_study: Production electrical model: supplies the tier-by-tier heat map to the CalculiX thermal solve at every electrothermal iteration and takes the temperatures back; the 48 V current is solved self-consistently.

tools.name: In-house E-T fixed-point driver
tools.developer: this study (in-house Python in this repository)
tools.what_it_is: The Python driver that alternates the electrical ledger and the CalculiX thermal solve until temperature and loss stop changing, then runs the mechanics once.
tools.quote: ledger(T) -> tier-aware heat map -> conjugate thermal FE -> T (repeat to a fixed point)
tools.source_note: in-house code: quoted from the repository source file, read on the date given
tools.role_in_study: Orchestrates the production chain: ledger(T) -> heat map -> CalculiX thermal -> T to the declared tolerances (ET_TOL_K, ET_TOL_P_REL in the script); then one CalculiX thermoelastic solve, the all-site joint search, and the hand-off of the critical joint to the local solder submodel.

tools.name: In-house package builders + YAML configs
tools.developer: this study (in-house Python and YAML in this repository)
tools.what_it_is: YAML files that describe the physical Z1 and Z2 packages, and the Python loader/builder that validates them and lays out layers, tiles and conductors.
tools.quote: So: ONE loader, ONE builder, and every physical number comes out of the YAML.
tools.source_note: in-house code: quoted from the repository source file, read on the date given
tools.role_in_study: Inputs: the physical package descriptions from which the FE meshes, the electrical ledger and the package network take their geometry.

tools.name: In-house structured hex mesher (etm.mesh)
tools.developer: this study (in-house Python in this repository)
tools.what_it_is: A Python mesher that builds conforming structured brick (hexahedral) meshes whose faces follow every material boundary and tile edge.
tools.quote: identical mesh for the thermal and structural passes, so the temperature field transfers node-to-node with zero interpolation error.
tools.source_note: in-house code: quoted from the repository source file, read on the date given
tools.role_in_study: Builds the C3D8 (thermal) / C3D8I (structural) meshes of the physical packages; production uses the h_xy = 1.1 mm grid with every in-plane interval split in two (r21), judged by a nested refinement study.

tools.name: Gmsh
tools.developer: Christophe Geuzaine and Jean-François Remacle
tools.what_it_is: An open-source 3-D finite element mesh generator with a built-in CAD engine and post-processor.
tools.quote: Gmsh is an open source 3D finite element mesh generator with a built-in CAD engine and post-processor.

supplementary_sources.quote: Gmsh is copyright (C) 1997-2026 by C. Geuzaine and J.-F. Remacle

tools.role_in_study: Generated the unstructured 2-D triangle meshes (MSH 2.2, three resolutions) of the package-RDL sheet for the MOOSE DC-analogue reference. Not used for the production meshes (etm.mesh), and not for the MOOSE thermal-column mesh, which in-house code writes directly in Gmsh's MSH 2.2 file format.

tools.name: MOOSE heat_transfer module (heat_transfer-opt)
tools.version_used: heat_transfer-opt, local build of MOOSE commit 09515f92aa (2026-07-09), in another user's tree
tools.developer: Idaho National Laboratory (primary developer)
tools.what_it_is: An open-source, parallel finite element multiphysics framework; its heat transfer module implements the heat conduction equation and its boundary conditions.
tools.quote: An open-source, parallel finite element framework

supplementary_sources.quote: The Multiphysics Object-Oriented Simulation Environment (MOOSE) is a finite-element, multiphysics framework primarily developed by Idaho National Laboratory.
The heat transfer module provides various implementations of the heat conduction equation, as well as associated boundary/interface conditions

tools.role_in_study: Independent open-source FE reference, never in the production path: (a) 3-D thermal column of one interior package cell (Z1, Z2) on MOOSE's own hex meshes at two resolutions, compared with CalculiX; (b) 2-D package-RDL DC conduction solved as the analogous heat-conduction problem on Gmsh meshes, compared with the in-house FV network.

tools.role_in_study: Commercial platform hosting the Mechanical design used for every Ansys reference solve (4 cores: solves requesting more fail without HPC licences). Q3D Extractor and Maxwell DC conduction are installed but not licensed; Icepak is licensed but its matched benchmark was not run.
tools.notes: The ansys.com product URL for Electronics Desktop redirected to the Ansys Electronics overview page on ansys.synopsys.com; the quotes are from its 'Ansys Electronics Desktop (AEDT)' section.

tools.name: AEDT Mechanical (thermal, structural)
tools.version_used: Mechanical design type of AEDT 2026 R1, solution types Thermal and Structural
tools.developer: Ansys (Mechanical design type inside Ansys Electronics Desktop)
tools.what_it_is: The Mechanical (thermal and structural finite element) application of Ansys Electronics Desktop, scripted through PyAEDT's Mechanical class.
tools.quote: Provides the Mechanical application interface.

supplementary_sources.quote: Assign a heat generation boundary condition to an object list.
Ansys Mechanical is a best-in-class finite element solver with structural, thermal, acoustics, transient and nonlinear capabilities to improve your modeling.

tools.role_in_study: Independent commercial FE reference (never production). Thermal: single-TSV DC resistance through the exact k<->sigma conduction analogy, TSV-tile k_z and k_xy, RDL-tier k_x and k_z unit cells, and the thermal column of one interior cell for Z1 and Z2. Structural: bilayer CTE-mismatch warpage from two solved temperature levels. Warm-up plus 3 timed repeats on 4 cores.
tools.notes: The ansys.com 'Ansys Mechanical' page describes Ansys's Mechanical product line; this study ran the Mechanical design type inside AEDT through PyAEDT. That page is recorded for context only and is not used to characterise the AEDT design type.

tools.developer: Ansys, PyAnsys project (documentation: "© Copyright 2026 Synopsys, Inc. and ANSYS, Inc.")
tools.what_it_is: A Python client library that drives the Ansys Electronics Desktop API so simulations can be scripted.
tools.quote: PyAEDT is a Python client library that interacts directly with the Ansys Electronics Desktop (AEDT) API, enabling straightforward and efficient automation in your workflow.

supplementary_sources.quote: © Copyright 2026 Synopsys, Inc. and ANSYS, Inc. All rights reserved.

tools.role_in_study: Builds, meshes, solves and post-processes every AEDT Mechanical reference model from Python; geometry images are exported from the same sessions with the native ExportModelImageToFile call.
tools.notes: The fetched documentation is the 'stable' PyAEDT 1.9.0 docs; the study used 1.1.0.

tools.name: Ansys Icepak
tools.version_used: installed and licensed with AEDT 2026 R1; not run for any study result
tools.developer: Ansys
tools.what_it_is: An Ansys electronics-cooling simulator (fluid flow and heat transfer) integrated in Electronics Desktop.
tools.quote: Ansys Icepak delivers high fidelity electrothermal and system level thermal simulation, along with structural analysis, using industry leading CFD and FEA solvers.

supplementary_sources.quote: Ansys Icepak simulates electronics cooling strategies and overall electronic dynamic thermal management for IC packages, PCB and electronic assemblies.

tools.role_in_study: Independent reference for the production cold-plate correlation: a conjugate CFD of one microchannel half-pitch (silicon fins, laminar water) at the production heat load; the correlation's temperature rise is 16.5 % above the CFD value (conservative), with a mesh change below 0.4 %.
tools.status_detail: Executed in the final closure: the matched conjugate-CFD benchmark of one cold-plate channel half-pitch, four mesh levels (research/final_closure/reference_cooling_icepak.json). An older manuscript sentence about a discarded earlier attempt refers to a different, historical setup.

tools.name: Ansys HFSS
tools.developer: Ansys
tools.what_it_is: An Ansys 3-D electromagnetic simulator for high-frequency electronic products.
tools.quote: Ansys HFSS is a 3D electromagnetic simulation software solution for designing and simulating high-frequency electronic products such as antennas, RF and microwave components, high-speed interconnects, filters, connectors, IC components and packages and printed circuit boards.
tools.role_in_study: Not part of the final-closure lineage. The manuscript states that a full-wave check of the via AC resistance was attempted and did not converge within budget, and claims no HFSS result; via frequency dependence comes from the analytic skin-depth model.
tools.status_detail: An earlier-phase HFSS script and outputs exist (scripts/phase0e/em_hfss.py, results/phase0e/aedt/); none is used in the final-closure results.
